subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core shell-facing `openclaw notify` admin broadcast surface now, fold it into the broader Control UI notification architecture, or leave shell-originated alerts to plugin/external delivery paths?
rationale: The requested capability is absent, but it creates a new admin-to-UI interruption path that crosses Gateway authorization, broadcast scoping, payload validation, UI policy, and overlapping notification work.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC, payload, and UI interruption contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Notifications
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 own the shared in-app notification architecture, then preserve this issue's shell/admin broadcast requirement as a scoped subtask or linked acceptance criterion.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Reject a core command and document the supported plugin, Web Push, channel, or node-notify path if maintainers decide shell-originated alerts should not directly interrupt Control UI sessions.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC, payload, and UI interruption contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest available history on Gateway broadcast scoping and related notification/product review context.
